                                                                                                                       | Provides a set of radio buttons based on the available options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }} |\n| inline-radio | Provides a set of inlined radio buttons based on the available options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'inline-radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                                |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| check        | Provides a set of checkbox components for selecting multiple options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                                         |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| inline-check | Provides a set of inlined checkbox components for selecting multiple options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'inline-check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                          |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| select       | Provides a drop-down list component to handle single value selection. argTypes: { age: { control: 'select', options: \\[20, 30, 40, 50\\] }}                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| multi-select | Provides a drop-down list that allows multiple selected values. argTypes: { countries: { control: 'multi-select', options: \\['USA', 'Canada', 'Mexico'\\] }}                                                     |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **string**   | text                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Provides a freeform text input. argTypes: { label: { control: 'text' }}                                                                           |\n| color        | Provides a color picker component to handle color values. Can be additionally configured to include a set of color presets. argTypes: { color: { control: { type: 'color', presetColors: \\['red', 'green'\\]} }} |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| date         | Provides a datepicker component to handle date selection. argTypes: { startDate: { control: 'date' }}                                                                                                           |                                                                                                                                                   |\n\n💡\n\nThe &#96;date&#96; control will convert the date into a UNIX timestamp when the value changes. It's a known limitation that will be fixed in a future release. If you need to represent the actual date, you'll need to update the story's implementation and convert the value into a date object.\n\nGizmo.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Gizmo } from './Gizmo';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Gizmo,\n  argTypes: {\n    canRotate: {\n      control: 'boolean',\n    },\n    width: {\n      control: { type: 'number', min: 400, max: 1200, step: 50 },\n    },\n    height: {\n      control: { type: 'range', min: 200, max: 1500, step: 50 },\n    },\n    rawData: {\n      control: 'object',\n    },\n    coordinates: {\n      control: 'object',\n    },\n    texture: {\n      control: {\n        type: 'file',\n        accept: '.png',\n      },\n    },\n    position: {\n      control: 'radio',\n      options: ['left', 'right', 'center'],\n    },\n    rotationAxis: {\n      control: 'check',\n      options: ['x', 'y', 'z'],\n    },\n    scaling: {\n      control: 'select',\n      options: [10, 50, 75, 100, 200],\n    },\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n    },\n    meshColors: {\n      control: {\n        type: 'color',\n        presetColors: ['#ff0000', '#00ff00', '#0000ff'],\n      },\n    },\n    revisionDate: {\n      control: 'date',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Gizmo\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nNumeric data types will default to a &#96;number&#96; control unless additional configuration is provided.\n\n### Parameters\n\nControls supports the following configuration parameters, either globally or on a per-story basis:\n\n#### Show full documentation for each property\n\nSince Controls is built on the same engine as Storybook Docs, it can also show property documentation alongside your controls using the expanded parameter (defaults to false). This means you embed a complete Controls doc block in the controls panel. The description and default value rendering can be customized like the doc block.\n\nTo enable expanded mode globally, add the following to .storybook/preview.js|ts:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { expanded: true },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nHere's what the resulting UI looks like:\n\nControls table expanded\n\n#### Specify initial preset color swatches\n\nFor &#96;color&#96; controls, you can specify an array of &#96;presetColors&#96;, either on the &#96;control&#96; in &#96;argTypes&#96;, or as a parameter under the &#96;controls&#96; namespace:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: {\n      presetColors: [{ color: '#ff4785', title: 'Coral' }, 'rgba(0, 159, 183, 1)', '#fe4a49'],\n    },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nColor presets can be defined as an object with &#96;color&#96; and &#96;title&#96; or a simple CSS color string. These will then be available as swatches in the color picker. When you hover over the color swatch, you'll be able to see its title. It will default to the nearest CSS color name if none is specified.\n\n#### Filtering controls\n\nIn specific cases, you may be required to display only a limited number of controls in the controls panel or all except a particular set.\n\nTo make this possible, you can use optional &#96;include&#96; and &#96;exclude&#96; configuration fields in the &#96;controls&#96; parameter, which you can define as an array of strings or a regular expression.\n\nConsider the following story snippets:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const ArrayInclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { include: ['foo', 'bar'] },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const RegexInclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { include: /^hello*/ },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const ArrayExclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { exclude: ['foo', 'bar'] },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const RegexExclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { exclude: /^hello*/ },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Sorting controls\n\nBy default, controls are unsorted and use whatever order the args data is processed in (&#96;none&#96;). Additionally, you can sort them alphabetically by the arg's name (&#96;alpha&#96;) or with the required args first (&#96;requiredFirst&#96;).\n\nConsider the following snippet to force required args first:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  parameters: { controls: { sort: 'requiredFirst' } },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Disable controls for specific properties\n\nAside from the features already documented here, Controls can also be disabled for individual properties.\n\nSuppose you want to turn off Controls for a property called &#96;foo&#96; in a component's story. The following example illustrates how:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  argTypes: {\n    // foo is the property we want to remove from the UI\n    foo: {\n      table: {\n        disable: true,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResulting in the following change in Storybook UI:\n\nThe previous example also removed the prop documentation from the table. In some cases, this is fine. However, sometimes you might want to render the prop documentation without a control. The following example illustrates how:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  argTypes: {\n    // foo is the property we want to remove from the UI\n    foo: {\n      control: false,\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nAs with other Storybook properties, such as decorators, you can apply the same pattern at a story level for more granular cases.\n\n### Conditional controls\n\nIn some cases, it's useful to be able to conditionally exclude a control based on the value of another control. Controls supports basic versions of these use cases with the &#96;if&#96;, which can take a simple query object to determine whether to include the control.\n\nConsider a collection of \"advanced\" settings only visible when the user toggles an \"advanced\" toggle.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    label: { control: 'text' }, // Always shows the control\n    advanced: { control: 'boolean' },\n    // Only enabled if advanced is true\n    margin: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n    padding: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n    cornerRadius: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr consider a constraint where if the user sets one control value, it doesn't make sense for the user to be able to set another value.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    // Button can be passed a label or an image, not both\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n      if: { arg: 'image', truthy: false },\n    },\n    image: {\n      control: { type: 'select', options: ['foo.jpg', 'bar.jpg'] },\n      if: { arg: 'label', truthy: false },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe query object must contain either an &#96;arg&#96; or &#96;global&#96; target:\n\n| field  | type   | meaning                       |\n| ------ | ------ | ----------------------------- |\n| arg    | string | The ID of the arg to test.    |\n| global | string | The ID of the global to test. |\n\nIt may also contain at most one of the following operators:\n\n| operator | type    | meaning                                              |\n| -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |\n| truthy   | boolean | Is the target value truthy?                          |\n| exists   | boolean | Is the target value defined?                         |\n| eq       | any     | Is the target value equal to the provided value?     |\n| neq      | any     | Is the target value NOT equal to the provided value? |\n\nIf no operator is provided, that is equivalent to &#96;{ truthy: true }&#96;.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### The controls are not updating the story within the auto-generated documentation\n\nIf you turned off inline rendering for your stories via the inline configuration option, you would run into a situation where the associated controls are not updating the story within the documentation page. This is a known limitation of the current implementation and will be addressed in a future release.\n\n## API\n\n### Parameters\n\nThis feature contributes the following parameters to Storybook, under the &#96;controls&#96; namespace:\n\n#### disable\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nDisable this feature's behavior. If you wish to disable this feature for the entire Storybook, you should do so in your main configuration file.\n\nThis parameter is most useful to allow overriding at more specific levels. For example, if this parameter is set to &#96;true&#96; at the project level, it could then be re-enabled by setting it to &#96;false&#96; at the meta (component) or story level.\n\n#### exclude\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nSpecifies which properties to exclude from the Controls panel. Any properties whose names match the regex or are part of the array will be left out. See usage example, above.\n\n#### expanded\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nShow the full documentation for each property in the Controls panel, including the description and default value. See usage example, above.\n\n#### include\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nSpecifies which properties to include in the Controls panel. Any properties whose names don't match the regex or are not part of the array will be left out. See usage example, above.\n\n#### presetColors\n\nType: &#96;(string | { color: string; title?: string })[]&#96;\n\nSpecify preset color swatches for the color picker control. The color value may be any valid CSS color. See usage example, above.\n\n#### sort\n\nType: &#96;'none' | 'alpha' | 'requiredFirst'&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;'none'&#96;\n\nSpecifies how the controls are sorted.\n\n* **none**: Unsorted, displayed in the same order the arg types are processed in\n* **alpha**: Sorted alphabetically, by the arg type's name\n* **requiredFirst**: Same as &#96;alpha&#96;, with any required arg types displayed first\n\n#### disableSaveFromUI\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;false&#96;\n\nDisable the ability to create or edit stories from the Controls panel.\n\nWas this page useful?\n\n👍👎\n\n✍️ Edit on Github\n\nOn this page\n\nJoin the community\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,044 developers and counting\n\nWhy\n\nWhy StorybookComponent driven UI\n\nDocs\n\nGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunity\n\nAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcase\n\nExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",

      "chunk": "Join us live: Automated vs Manual—The right A11y Testing Mix\n\n* Docs\n* Addons\n* Showcase\n* Blog\n* Visual Test\n* Enterprise\n\n87,387\n\nSearch docs\n\nDocs \n\nStorybook Browse stories  \n   * Setup  \n   * Conclusion\n* Stories  \n   * Args  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Decorators  \n   * Play function  \n   * Loaders  \n   * Tags  \n   * Naming components and hierarchy  \n   * Mocking data and modules  \n   * Building pages and screens  \n   * Stories for multiple components  \n   * Writing stories in TypeScript\n* Testing  \n   * Interaction tests  \n   * Accessibility tests  \n   * Visual tests  \n   * Snapshot tests  \n   * Test coverage  \n   * In CI  \n   * Integrations\n* Docs  \n   * Autodocs  \n   * MDX  \n   * Doc blocks  \n   * Code panel  \n Controls  \n   * Highlight  \n   * Measure \u0026 outline  \n   * Toolbars \u0026 globals  \n   * Viewport\n* Addons  \n   * Install  \n   * Write  \n   * Configure addons  \n   * Write a preset  \n   * Add to catalog  \n   * Types of addons  \n   * Knowledge base  \n   * Addon API  \n   * Migrate addons to 9.0\n* Configure  \n   * Styling and CSS  \n   * Telemetry  \n   * Integration  \n   * Story rendering  \n   * Story layout  \n   * User Interface  \n   * Environment variables\n* Builders  \n   * Vite  \n   * Webpack  \n   * API\n* API  \n   * main.js|ts configuration  \n   * Component Story Format (CSF)  \n   * ArgTypes  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Doc Blocks  \n   * Portable Stories  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * CLI options\n* Releases  \n   * Migrate to Storybook 9  \n   * Migrate from 7 to 8  \n   * Upgrading  \n   * Feature Lifecycle  \n   * Roadmap\n* Contribute  \n   * RFC process  \n   * Code  \n   * Documentation  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * Reproduce\n* FAQ\n\n# Controls\n\nReactVueAngularWeb ComponentsMore\n\nStorybook Controls gives you a graphical UI to interact with a component's arguments dynamically without needing to code. Use the Controls panel to edit the inputs to your stories and see the results in real-time. It's a great way to explore your components and test different states.\n\nControls do not require any modification to your components. Stories for controls are:\n\n* Convenient. Auto-generate controls based on React/Vue/Angular/etc. components.\n* Portable. Reuse your interactive stories in documentation, tests, and even in designs.\n* Rich. Customize the controls and interactive data to suit your exact needs.\n\nTo use Controls, you need to write your stories using args. Storybook will automatically generate UI controls based on your args and what it can infer about your component. Still, you can configure the controls further using argTypes, see below.\n\n💡\n\nIf you have stories in the older pre-Storybook 6 style, check the args \u0026 controls migration guide to learn how to convert your existing stories for args.\n\n## Choosing the control type\n\nBy default, Storybook will choose a control for each arg based on its initial value. This will work well with specific arg types (e.g., &#96;boolean&#96; or &#96;string&#96;). To enable them, add the &#96;component&#96; annotation to the default export of your story file, and it will be used to infer the controls and auto-generate the matching argTypes for your component using react-docgen, a documentation generator for React components that also includes first-class support for TypeScript.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, nextjs-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor instance, suppose you have a &#96;variant&#96; arg on your story that should be &#96;primary&#96; or &#96;secondary&#96;:\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const Primary: Story = {\n  args: {\n    variant: 'primary',\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy default, Storybook will render a free text input for the &#96;variant&#96; arg:\n\nControl using a string\n\nIt works as long as you type a valid string into the auto-generated text control. Still, it's not the best UI for our scenario, given that the component only accepts &#96;primary&#96; or &#96;secondary&#96; as variants. Let’s replace it with Storybook’s radio component.\n\nWe can specify which controls get used by declaring a custom argType for the &#96;variant&#96; property. ArgTypes encode basic metadata for args, such as name, description, and defaultValue for an arg. These get automatically filled in by Storybook Docs.\n\n&#96;ArgTypes&#96; can also contain arbitrary annotations, which the user can override. Since &#96;variant&#96; is a component property, let's put that annotation on the default export.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    variant: {\n      options: ['primary', 'secondary'],\n      control: { type: 'radio' },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nArgTypes are a powerful feature that can be used to customize the controls for your stories. For more information, see the documentation about customizing controls with &#96;argTypes&#96; annotation.\n\nThis replaces the input with a radio group for a more intuitive experience.\n\nControl with a radio group\n\n## Custom control type matchers\n\nControls can automatically be inferred from arg's name with regex, but currently only for the color picker and date picker controls. If you've used the Storybook CLI to setup your project, it should have automatically created the following defaults in &#96;.storybook/preview.js|ts&#96;:\n\n| Control   | Default regex           | Description                                               |\n| --------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **color** | /(background\\|color)$/i | Will display a color picker UI for the args that match it |\n| **date**  | /Date$/                 | Will display a date picker UI for the args that match it  |\n\nIf you haven't used the CLI to set the configuration, or if you want to define your patterns, use the &#96;matchers&#96; property in the &#96;controls&#96; parameter:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: {\n      matchers: {\n        color: /(background|color)$/i,\n        date: /Date$/,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Fully custom args\n\nUntil now, we only used auto-generated controls based on the component for which we're writing stories. If we are writing complex stories, we may want to add controls for args that aren’t part of the component. For example, here's how you could use a &#96;footer&#96; arg to populate a child component:\n\nPage.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, nextjs-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Page } from './Page';\n \ntype PagePropsAndCustomArgs = React.ComponentProps\u003ctypeof Page\u003e \u0026 { footer?: string };\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Page,\n  render: ({ footer, ...args }) =\u003e (\n    \u003cPage {...args}\u003e\n      \u003cfooter\u003e{footer}\u003c/footer\u003e\n    \u003c/Page\u003e\n  ),\n} satisfies Meta\u003cPagePropsAndCustomArgs\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n \ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const CustomFooter = {\n  args: {\n    footer: 'Built with Storybook',\n  },\n} satisfies Story;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy default, Storybook will add controls for all args that:\n\n* It infers from the component definition if your framework supports it.\n* Appear in the list of args for your story.\n\nUsing &#96;argTypes&#96;, you can change the display and behavior of each control.\n\n### Dealing with complex values\n\nWhen dealing with non-primitive values, you'll notice that you'll run into some limitations. The most obvious issue is that not every value can be represented as part of the &#96;args&#96; param in the URL, losing the ability to share and deep link to such a state. Beyond that, complex values such as JSX cannot be synchronized between the manager (e.g., the Controls panel) and the preview (your story).\n\nOne way to deal with this is to use primitive values (e.g., strings) as arg values and add a custom &#96;render&#96; function to convert them to their complex counterpart before rendering. It isn't the nicest way to do it (see below), but certainly the most flexible.\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, nextjs-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './your-component';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  //👇 Creates specific argTypes with options\n  argTypes: {\n    propertyA: {\n      options: ['Item One', 'Item Two', 'Item Three'],\n      control: { type: 'select' }, // Automatically inferred when 'options' is defined\n    },\n    propertyB: {\n      options: ['Another Item One', 'Another Item Two', 'Another Item Three'],\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nconst someFunction = (valuePropertyA, valuePropertyB) =\u003e {\n  // Do some logic here\n};\n \nexport const ExampleStory: Story = {\n  render: (args) =\u003e {\n    const { propertyA, propertyB } = args;\n    //👇 Assigns the function result to a variable\n    const someFunctionResult = someFunction(propertyA, propertyB);\n \n    return \u003cYourComponent {...args} someProperty={someFunctionResult} /\u003e;\n  },\n  args: {\n    propertyA: 'Item One',\n    propertyB: 'Another Item One',\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUnless you need the flexibility of a function, an easier way to map primitives to complex values before rendering is to define a &#96;mapping&#96;; additionally, you can specify &#96;control.labels&#96; to configure custom labels for your checkbox, radio, or select input.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nimport { ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight } from './icons';\n \nconst arrows = { ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight };\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    arrow: {\n      options: Object.keys(arrows), // An array of serializable values\n      mapping: arrows, // Maps serializable option values to complex arg values\n      control: {\n        type: 'select', // Type 'select' is automatically inferred when 'options' is defined\n        labels: {\n          // 'labels' maps option values to string labels\n          ArrowUp: 'Up',\n          ArrowDown: 'Down',\n          ArrowLeft: 'Left',\n          ArrowRight: 'Right',\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that both &#96;mapping&#96; and &#96;control.labels&#96; don't have to be exhaustive. If the currently selected option is not listed, it's used verbatim.\n\n## Creating and editing stories from controls\n\nYou can create or edit stories, directly from the Controls panel.\n\n### Create a new story\n\nOpen the Controls panel for a story and adjust the value of a control. Then save those changes as a new story.\n\nIf you're working on a component that does not yet have any stories, you can click the ➕ button in the sidebar to search for your component and have a basic story created for you.\n\n### Edit a story\n\nYou can also update a control's value, then save the changes to the story. The story file's code will be updated for you.\n\n### Disable creating and editing of stories\n\nIf you don't want to allow the creation or editing of stories from the Controls panel, you can disable this feature by setting the &#96;disableSaveFromUI&#96; parameter to &#96;true&#96; in the &#96;parameters.controls&#96; parameter in your &#96;.storybook/preview.js|ts&#96; file.\n\n## Configuration\n\nControls can be configured in two ways:\n\n* Individual controls can be configured via control annotations.\n* The panel's appearance can be configured via parameters.\n\n### Annotation\n\nAs shown above, you can configure individual controls with the “control\" annotation in the argTypes field of either a component or story. Below is a condensed example and table featuring all available controls.\n\n| Data Type    | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                       |\n| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **boolean**  | boolean                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Provides a toggle for switching between possible states. argTypes: { active: { control: 'boolean' }}                                              |\n| **number**   | number                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Provides a numeric input to include the range of all possible values. argTypes: { even: { control: { type: 'number', min:1, max:30, step: 2 } }}  |\n| range        | Provides a range slider component to include all possible values. argTypes: { odd: { control: { type: 'range', min: 1, max: 30, step: 3 } }}                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **object**   | object                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Provides a JSON-based editor component to handle the object's values. Also allows edition in raw mode. argTypes: { user: { control: 'object' }}   |\n| **array**    | object                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Provides a JSON-based editor component to handle the array's values. Also allows edition in raw mode. argTypes: { odd: { control: 'object' }}     |\n| file         | Provides a file input component that returns an array of URLs. Can be further customized to accept specific file types. argTypes: { avatar: { control: { type: 'file', accept: '.png' } }}                      |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **enum**     | radio                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Provides a set of radio buttons based on the available options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }} |\n| inline-radio | Provides a set of inlined radio buttons based on the available options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'inline-radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                                |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| check        | Provides a set of checkbox components for selecting multiple options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                                         |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| inline-check | Provides a set of inlined checkbox components for selecting multiple options. argTypes: { contact: { control: 'inline-check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }}                                          |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| select       | Provides a drop-down list component to handle single value selection. argTypes: { age: { control: 'select', options: \\[20, 30, 40, 50\\] }}                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| multi-select | Provides a drop-down list that allows multiple selected values. argTypes: { countries: { control: 'multi-select', options: \\['USA', 'Canada', 'Mexico'\\] }}                                                     |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **string**   | text                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Provides a freeform text input. argTypes: { label: { control: 'text' }}                                                                           |\n| color        | Provides a color picker component to handle color values. Can be additionally configured to include a set of color presets. argTypes: { color: { control: { type: 'color', presetColors: \\['red', 'green'\\]} }} |                                                                                                                                                   |\n| date         | Provides a datepicker component to handle date selection. argTypes: { startDate: { control: 'date' }}                                                                                                           |                                                                                                                                                   |\n\n💡\n\nThe &#96;date&#96; control will convert the date into a UNIX timestamp when the value changes. It's a known limitation that will be fixed in a future release. If you need to represent the actual date, you'll need to update the story's implementation and convert the value into a date object.\n\nGizmo.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Gizmo } from './Gizmo';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Gizmo,\n  argTypes: {\n    canRotate: {\n      control: 'boolean',\n    },\n    width: {\n      control: { type: 'number', min: 400, max: 1200, step: 50 },\n    },\n    height: {\n      control: { type: 'range', min: 200, max: 1500, step: 50 },\n    },\n    rawData: {\n      control: 'object',\n    },\n    coordinates: {\n      control: 'object',\n    },\n    texture: {\n      control: {\n        type: 'file',\n        accept: '.png',\n      },\n    },\n    position: {\n      control: 'radio',\n      options: ['left', 'right', 'center'],\n    },\n    rotationAxis: {\n      control: 'check',\n      options: ['x', 'y', 'z'],\n    },\n    scaling: {\n      control: 'select',\n      options: [10, 50, 75, 100, 200],\n    },\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n    },\n    meshColors: {\n      control: {\n        type: 'color',\n        presetColors: ['#ff0000', '#00ff00', '#0000ff'],\n      },\n    },\n    revisionDate: {\n      control: 'date',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Gizmo\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nNumeric data types will default to a &#96;number&#96; control unless additional configuration is provided.\n\n### Parameters\n\nControls supports the following configuration parameters, either globally or on a per-story basis:\n\n#### Show full documentation for each property\n\nSince Controls is built on the same engine as Storybook Docs, it can also show property documentation alongside your controls using the expanded parameter (defaults to false). This means you embed a complete Controls doc block in the controls panel. The description and default value rendering can be customized like the doc block.\n\nTo enable expanded mode globally, add the following to .storybook/preview.js|ts:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { expanded: true },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nHere's what the resulting UI looks like:\n\nControls table expanded\n\n#### Specify initial preset color swatches\n\nFor &#96;color&#96; controls, you can specify an array of &#96;presetColors&#96;, either on the &#96;control&#96; in &#96;argTypes&#96;, or as a parameter under the &#96;controls&#96; namespace:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: {\n      presetColors: [{ color: '#ff4785', title: 'Coral' }, 'rgba(0, 159, 183, 1)', '#fe4a49'],\n    },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nColor presets can be defined as an object with &#96;color&#96; and &#96;title&#96; or a simple CSS color string. These will then be available as swatches in the color picker. When you hover over the color swatch, you'll be able to see its title. It will default to the nearest CSS color name if none is specified.\n\n#### Filtering controls\n\nIn specific cases, you may be required to display only a limited number of controls in the controls panel or all except a particular set.\n\nTo make this possible, you can use optional &#96;include&#96; and &#96;exclude&#96; configuration fields in the &#96;controls&#96; parameter, which you can define as an array of strings or a regular expression.\n\nConsider the following story snippets:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const ArrayInclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { include: ['foo', 'bar'] },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const RegexInclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { include: /^hello*/ },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const ArrayExclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { exclude: ['foo', 'bar'] },\n  },\n};\n \nexport const RegexExclude: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    controls: { exclude: /^hello*/ },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Sorting controls\n\nBy default, controls are unsorted and use whatever order the args data is processed in (&#96;none&#96;). Additionally, you can sort them alphabetically by the arg's name (&#96;alpha&#96;) or with the required args first (&#96;requiredFirst&#96;).\n\nConsider the following snippet to force required args first:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  parameters: { controls: { sort: 'requiredFirst' } },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Disable controls for specific properties\n\nAside from the features already documented here, Controls can also be disabled for individual properties.\n\nSuppose you want to turn off Controls for a property called &#96;foo&#96; in a component's story. The following example illustrates how:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  argTypes: {\n    // foo is the property we want to remove from the UI\n    foo: {\n      table: {\n        disable: true,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResulting in the following change in Storybook UI:\n\nThe previous example also removed the prop documentation from the table. In some cases, this is fine. However, sometimes you might want to render the prop documentation without a control. The following example illustrates how:\n\nYourComponent.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { YourComponent } from './YourComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: YourComponent,\n  argTypes: {\n    // foo is the property we want to remove from the UI\n    foo: {\n      control: false,\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof YourComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nAs with other Storybook properties, such as decorators, you can apply the same pattern at a story level for more granular cases.\n\n### Conditional controls\n\nIn some cases, it's useful to be able to conditionally exclude a control based on the value of another control. Controls supports basic versions of these use cases with the &#96;if&#96;, which can take a simple query object to determine whether to include the control.\n\nConsider a collection of \"advanced\" settings only visible when the user toggles an \"advanced\" toggle.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    label: { control: 'text' }, // Always shows the control\n    advanced: { control: 'boolean' },\n    // Only enabled if advanced is true\n    margin: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n    padding: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n    cornerRadius: { control: 'number', if: { arg: 'advanced' } },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr consider a constraint where if the user sets one control value, it doesn't make sense for the user to be able to set another value.\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    // Button can be passed a label or an image, not both\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n      if: { arg: 'image', truthy: false },\n    },\n    image: {\n      control: { type: 'select', options: ['foo.jpg', 'bar.jpg'] },\n      if: { arg: 'label', truthy: false },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe query object must contain either an &#96;arg&#96; or &#96;global&#96; target:\n\n| field  | type   | meaning                       |\n| ------ | ------ | ----------------------------- |\n| arg    | string | The ID of the arg to test.    |\n| global | string | The ID of the global to test. |\n\nIt may also contain at most one of the following operators:\n\n| operator | type    | meaning                                              |\n| -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |\n| truthy   | boolean | Is the target value truthy?                          |\n| exists   | boolean | Is the target value defined?                         |\n| eq       | any     | Is the target value equal to the provided value?     |\n| neq      | any     | Is the target value NOT equal to the provided value? |\n\nIf no operator is provided, that is equivalent to &#96;{ truthy: true }&#96;.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### The controls are not updating the story within the auto-generated documentation\n\nIf you turned off inline rendering for your stories via the inline configuration option, you would run into a situation where the associated controls are not updating the story within the documentation page. This is a known limitation of the current implementation and will be addressed in a future release.\n\n## API\n\n### Parameters\n\nThis feature contributes the following parameters to Storybook, under the &#96;controls&#96; namespace:\n\n#### disable\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nDisable this feature's behavior. If you wish to disable this feature for the entire Storybook, you should do so in your main configuration file.\n\nThis parameter is most useful to allow overriding at more specific levels. For example, if this parameter is set to &#96;true&#96; at the project level, it could then be re-enabled by setting it to &#96;false&#96; at the meta (component) or story level.\n\n#### exclude\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nSpecifies which properties to exclude from the Controls panel. Any properties whose names match the regex or are part of the array will be left out. See usage example, above.\n\n#### expanded\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nShow the full documentation for each property in the Controls panel, including the description and default value. See usage example, above.\n\n#### include\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nSpecifies which properties to include in the Controls panel. Any properties whose names don't match the regex or are not part of the array will be left out. See usage example, above.\n\n#### presetColors\n\nType: &#96;(string | { color: string; title?: string })[]&#96;\n\nSpecify preset color swatches for the color picker control. The color value may be any valid CSS color. See usage example, above.\n\n#### sort\n\nType: &#96;'none' | 'alpha' | 'requiredFirst'&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;'none'&#96;\n\nSpecifies how the controls are sorted.\n\n* **none**: Unsorted, displayed in the same order the arg types are processed in\n* **alpha**: Sorted alphabetically, by the arg type's name\n* **requiredFirst**: Same as &#96;alpha&#96;, with any required arg types displayed first\n\n#### disableSaveFromUI\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;false&#96;\n\nDisable the ability to create or edit stories from the Controls panel.\n\nWas this page useful?\n\n👍👎\n\n✍️ Edit on Github\n\nOn this page\n\nJoin the community\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,044 developers and counting\n\nWhy\n\nWhy StorybookComponent driven UI\n\nDocs\n\nGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunity\n\nAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcase\n\nExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",

      "chunk": "Join us live: Automated vs Manual—The right A11y Testing Mix\n\n* Docs\n* Addons\n* Showcase\n* Blog\n* Visual Test\n* Enterprise\n\n87,387\n\nSearch docs\n\nDocs \n\nStorybook DocsDocs » API » ArgTypes\n\nDocumentationAPITutorialsAddonsChangelog\n\nVersion 9.1\n* Get Started  \n   * Why Storybook?  \n   * Install  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * What's a story?  \n   * Browse stories  \n   * Setup  \n   * Conclusion\n* Stories  \n   * Args  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Decorators  \n   * Play function  \n   * Loaders  \n   * Tags  \n   * Naming components and hierarchy  \n   * Mocking data and modules  \n   * Building pages and screens  \n   * Stories for multiple components  \n   * Writing stories in TypeScript\n* Testing  \n   * Interaction tests  \n   * Accessibility tests  \n   * Visual tests  \n   * Snapshot tests  \n   * Test coverage  \n   * In CI  \n   * Integrations\n* Docs  \n   * Autodocs  \n   * MDX  \n   * Doc blocks  \n   * Code panel  \n   * Preview and build docs\n* Sharing  \n   * Publish  \n   * Embed  \n   * Design integrations  \n   * Composition  \n   * Package Composition\n* Essentials  \n   * Actions  \n   * Backgrounds  \n   * Controls  \n   * Highlight  \n   * Measure \u0026 outline  \n   * Toolbars \u0026 globals  \n   * Viewport\n* Addons  \n   * Install  \n   * Write  \n   * Configure addons  \n   * Write a preset  \n   * Add to catalog  \n   * Types of addons  \n   * Knowledge base  \n   * Addon API  \n   * Migrate addons to 9.0\n* Configure  \n   * Styling and CSS  \n   * Telemetry  \n   * Integration  \n   * Story rendering  \n   * Story layout  \n   * User Interface  \n   * Environment variables\n* Builders  \n   * Vite  \n   * Webpack  \n   * API\n* API  \n   * main.js|ts configuration  \n   * Component Story Format (CSF)  \n   * ArgTypes  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Doc Blocks  \n   * Portable Stories  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * CLI options\n* Releases  \n   * Migrate to Storybook 9  \n   * Migrate from 7 to 8  \n   * Upgrading  \n   * Feature Lifecycle  \n   * Roadmap\n* Contribute  \n   * RFC process  \n   * Code  \n   * Documentation  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * Reproduce\n* FAQ\n\n# ArgTypes\n\nReactVueAngularWeb ComponentsMore\n\nArgTypes specify the behavior of args. By specifying the type of an arg, you constrain the values that it can accept and provide information about args that are not explicitly set (i.e., description).\n\nYou can also use argTypes to “annotate” args with information used by addons that make use of those args. For instance, to instruct the controls panel to render a color picker, you could specify the &#96;'color'&#96; control type.\n\nThe most concrete realization of argTypes is the ArgTypes doc block (Controls is similar). Each row in the table corresponds to a single argType and the current value of that arg.\n\nArgTypes table\n\n## Automatic argType inference\n\nIf you are using the Storybook docs addon, then Storybook will infer a set of argTypes for each story based on the &#96;component&#96; specified in the default export of the CSF file.\n\nTo do so, Storybook uses various static analysis tools depending on your framework.\n\n| Framework     | Static analysis tool                                                                                                                                    |\n| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| React         | [react-docgen](https://github.com/reactjs/react-docgen) (default) or [react-docgen-typescript](https://github.com/styleguidist/react-docgen-typescript) |\n| Vue           | [vue-docgen-api](https://github.com/vue-styleguidist/vue-styleguidist/tree/dev/packages/vue-docgen-api)                                                 |\n| Angular       | [compodoc](https://compodoc.app/)                                                                                                                       |\n| WebComponents | [custom-element.json](https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-json)                                                                            |\n| Ember         | [YUI doc](https://github.com/ember-learn/ember-cli-addon-docs-yuidoc#documenting-components)                                                            |\n\nThe data structure of &#96;argTypes&#96; is designed to match the output of the these tools. Properties specified manually will override what is inferred.\n\n## Manually specifying argTypes\n\nFor most Storybook projects, argTypes are automatically inferred from your components. Any argTypes specified manually will override the inferred values.\n\nArgTypes are most often specified at the meta (component) level, in the default export of the CSF file:\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  argTypes: {\n    // 👇 All Button stories expect a label arg\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n      description: 'Overwritten description',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThey can apply to all stories when specified at the project (global) level, in the &#96;preview.js|ts&#96; configuration file:\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview = {\n  argTypes: {\n    // 👇 All stories expect a label arg\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n      description: 'Overwritten description',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Preview;\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr they can apply only to a specific story:\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const Basic: Story = {\n  argTypes: {\n    // 👇 This story expects a label arg\n    label: {\n      control: 'text',\n      description: 'Overwritten description',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Story;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## argTypes\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  [key: string]: {\n    control?: ControlType | { type: ControlType; /* See below for more */ } | false;\n    description?: string;\n    if?: Conditional;\n    mapping?: { [key: string]: { [option: string]: any } };\n    name?: string;\n    options?: string[];\n    table?: {\n      category?: string;\n      defaultValue?: { summary: string; detail?: string };\n      disable?: boolean;\n      subcategory?: string;\n      type?: { summary?: string; detail?: string };\n    },\n    type?: SBType | SBScalarType['name'];\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou configure argTypes using an object with keys matching the name of args. The value of each key is an object with the following properties:\n\n### control\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n| ControlType\n| {\n    type: ControlType,\n    accept?: string;\n    labels?: { [option: string]: string };\n    max?: number;\n    min?: number;\n    presetColors?: string[];\n    step?: number;\n  }\n| false\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nDefault:\n\n1. &#96;'select'&#96;, if options are specified\n2. Else, inferred from type\n3. Else, &#96;'object'&#96;\n\nSpecify the behavior of the controls panel for the arg. If you specify a string, it's used as the type of the control. If you specify an object, you can provide additional configuration. Specifying &#96;false&#96; will prevent the control from rendering.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    value: {\n      control: {\n        type: 'number',\n        min: 0,\n        max: 100,\n        step: 10,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### control.type\n\nType: &#96;ControlType | null&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred; &#96;'select'&#96;, if options are specified; falling back to &#96;'object'&#96;\n\nSpecifies the type of control used to change the arg value with the controls panel. Here are the available types, &#96;ControlType&#96;, grouped by the type of data they handle:\n\n| Data type      | ControlType                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                       |\n| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **array**      | 'object'                                                                                                                                   | Provides a JSON-based editor to handle the values of the array. Also allows editing in raw mode. { control: 'object' }                                                            |\n| **boolean**    | 'boolean'                                                                                                                                  | Provides a toggle for switching between possible states. { control: 'boolean' }                                                                                                   |\n| **enum**       | 'check'                                                                                                                                    | Provides a set of stacked checkboxes for selecting multiple options. { control: 'check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }                                                  |\n| 'inline-check' | Provides a set of inlined checkboxes for selecting multiple options. { control: 'inline-check', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }    |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| 'radio'        | Provides a set of stacked radio buttons based on the available options. { control: 'radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] }        |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| 'inline-radio' | Provides a set of inlined radio buttons based on the available options. { control: 'inline-radio', options: \\['email', 'phone', 'mail'\\] } |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| 'select'       | Provides a select to choose a single value from the options. { control: 'select', options: \\[20, 30, 40, 50\\] }                            |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| 'multi-select' | Provides a select to choose multiple values from the options. { control: 'multi-select', options: \\['USA', 'Canada', 'Mexico'\\] }          |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **number**     | 'number'                                                                                                                                   | Provides a numeric input to include the range of all possible values. { control: { type: 'number', min:1, max:30, step: 2 } }                                                     |\n| 'range'        | Provides a range slider to include all possible values. { control: { type: 'range', min: 1, max: 30, step: 3 } }                           |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **object**     | 'file'                                                                                                                                     | Provides a file input that returns an array of URLs. Can be further customized to accept specific file types. { control: { type: 'file', accept: '.png' } }                       |\n| 'object'       | Provides a JSON-based editor to handle the object's values. Also allows editing in raw mode. { control: 'object' }                         |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| **string**     | 'color'                                                                                                                                    | Provides a color picker to choose color values. Can be additionally configured to include a set of color presets. { control: { type: 'color', presetColors: \\['red', 'green'\\]} } |\n| 'date'         | Provides a datepicker to choose a date. { control: 'date' }                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| 'text'         | Provides a freeform text input. { control: 'text' }                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n\n💡\n\nThe &#96;date&#96; control will convert the date into a UNIX timestamp when the value changes. It's a known limitation that will be fixed in a future release. If you need to represent the actual date, you'll need to update the story's implementation and convert the value into a date object.\n\n#### control.accept\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nWhen &#96;type&#96; is &#96;'file'&#96;, you can specify the file types that are accepted. The value should be a string of comma-separated MIME types.\n\n#### control.labels\n\nType: &#96;{ [option: string]: string }&#96;\n\nMap options to labels. &#96;labels&#96; doesn't have to be exhaustive. If an option is not in the object's keys, it's used verbatim.\n\n#### control.max\n\nType: &#96;number&#96;\n\nWhen &#96;type&#96; is &#96;'number'&#96; or &#96;'range'&#96;, sets the maximum allowed value.\n\n#### control.min\n\nType: &#96;number&#96;\n\nWhen &#96;type&#96; is &#96;'number'&#96; or &#96;'range'&#96;, sets the minimum allowed value.\n\n#### control.presetColors\n\nType: &#96;string[]&#96;\n\nWhen &#96;type&#96; is &#96;'color'&#96;, defines the set of colors that are available in addition to the general color picker. The values in the array should be valid CSS color values.\n\n#### control.step\n\nType: &#96;number&#96;\n\nWhen &#96;type&#96; is &#96;'number'&#96; or &#96;'range'&#96;, sets the granularity allowed when incrementing/decrementing the value.\n\n### description\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred\n\nDescribe the arg. (If you intend to describe the type of the arg, you should use table.type, instead.)\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    value: {\n      description: 'The value of the slider',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### if\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  [predicateType: 'arg' | 'global']: string;\n  eq?: any;\n  exists?: boolean;\n  neq?: any;\n  truthy?: boolean;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nConditionally render an argType based on the value of another arg or global.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    parent: { control: 'select', options: ['one', 'two', 'three'] },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg exists\n    parentExists: { if: { arg: 'parent', exists: true } },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg does not exist\n    parentDoesNotExist: { if: { arg: 'parent', exists: false } },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg value is truthy\n    parentIsTruthy: { if: { arg: 'parent' } },\n    parentIsTruthyVerbose: { if: { arg: 'parent', truthy: true } },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg value is not truthy\n    parentIsNotTruthy: { if: { arg: 'parent', truthy: false } },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg value is 'three'\n    parentIsEqToValue: { if: { arg: 'parent', eq: 'three' } },\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;parent&#96; arg value is not 'three'\n    parentIsNotEqToValue: { if: { arg: 'parent', neq: 'three' } },\n \n    // Each of the above can also be conditional on the value of a globalType, e.g.:\n \n    // 👇 Only shown when &#96;theme&#96; global exists\n    parentExists: { if: { global: 'theme', exists: true } },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### mapping\n\nType: &#96;{ [key: string]: { [option: string]: any } }&#96;\n\nMap options to values.\n\nWhen dealing with non-primitive values, you'll notice that you'll run into some limitations. The most obvious issue is that not every value can be represented as part of the &#96;args&#96; param in the URL, losing the ability to share and deeplink to such a state. Beyond that, complex values such as JSX cannot be synchronized between the manager (e.g., Controls panel) and the preview (your story).\n\n&#96;mapping&#96; doesn't have to be exhaustive. If the currently selected option is not listed, it's used verbatim. Can be used with control.labels.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    label: {\n      control: { type: 'select' },\n      options: ['Normal', 'Bold', 'Italic'],\n      mapping: {\n        Bold: \u003cb\u003eBold\u003c/b\u003e,\n        Italic: \u003ci\u003eItalic\u003c/i\u003e,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### name\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nThe &#96;argTypes&#96; object uses the name of the arg as the key. By default, that key is used when displaying the argType in Storybook. You can override the displayed name by specifying a &#96;name&#96; property.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    actualArgName: {\n      name: 'Friendly name',\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n⚠️\n\nBe careful renaming args in this way. Users of the component you're documenting will not be able to use the documented name as a property of your component and the actual name will not displayed.\n\nFor this reason, the &#96;name&#96; property is best used when defining an &#96;argType&#96; that is only used for documentation purposes and not an actual property of the component. For example, when providing argTypes for each property of an object.\n\n### options\n\nType: &#96;string[]&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred\n\nIf the arg accepts a finite set of values, you can specify them with &#96;options&#96;. If those values are complex, like JSX elements, you can use mapping to map them to string values. You can use control.labels to provide custom labels for the options.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    icon: {\n      options: ['arrow-up', 'arrow-down', 'loading'],\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### table\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  category?: string;\n  defaultValue?: {\n    detail?: string;\n    summary: string;\n  };\n  disable?: boolean;\n  subcategory?: string;\n  type?: {\n    detail?: string;\n    summary: string;\n  };\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred\n\nSpecify how the arg is documented in the ArgTypes doc block, Controls doc block, and Controls panel.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    value: {\n      table: {\n        defaultValue: { summary: 0 },\n        type: { summary: 'number' },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### table.category\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred, in some frameworks\n\nDisplay the argType under a category heading, with the label specified by &#96;category&#96;.\n\n#### table.defaultValue\n\nType: &#96;{ detail?: string; summary: string }&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred\n\nThe documented default value of the argType. &#96;summary&#96; is typically used for the value itself, while &#96;detail&#96; is used for additional information.\n\n#### table.disable\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nSet to &#96;true&#96; to remove the argType's row from the table.\n\n#### table.readonly\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nSet to &#96;true&#96; to indicate that the argType is read-only.\n\n#### table.subcategory\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nDisplay the argType under a subcategory heading (which displays under the \\[&#96;category&#96;\\] heading), with the label specified by &#96;subcategory&#96;.\n\n#### table.type\n\nType: &#96;{ detail?: string; summary: string }&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred from type\n\nThe documented type of the argType. &#96;summary&#96; is typically used for the type itself, while &#96;detail&#96; is used for additional information.\n\nIf you need to specify the actual, semantic type, you should use type, instead.\n\n### type\n\nType: &#96;'boolean' | 'function' | 'number' | 'string' | 'symbol' | SBType&#96;\n\nThe full type of &#96;SBType&#96; is:\n\nSBType\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ninterface SBBaseType {\n  required?: boolean;\n  raw?: string;\n}\n \ntype SBScalarType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'boolean' | 'string' | 'number' | 'function' | 'symbol';\n};\n \ntype SBArrayType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'array';\n  value: SBType;\n};\ntype SBObjectType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'object';\n  value: Record\u003cstring, SBType\u003e;\n};\ntype SBEnumType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'enum';\n  value: (string | number)[];\n};\ntype SBIntersectionType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'intersection';\n  value: SBType[];\n};\ntype SBUnionType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'union';\n  value: SBType[];\n};\ntype SBOtherType = SBBaseType \u0026 {\n  name: 'other';\n  value: string;\n};\n \ntype SBType =\n  | SBScalarType\n  | SBEnumType\n  | SBArrayType\n  | SBObjectType\n  | SBIntersectionType\n  | SBUnionType\n  | SBOtherType;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nDefault: Inferred\n\nSpecifies the semantic type of the argType. When an argType is inferred, the information from the various tools is summarized in this property, which is then used to infer other properties, like control and table.type.\n\nIf you only need to specify the documented type, you should use table.type, instead.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    value: { type: 'number' },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### defaultValue\n\n(⛔️ **Deprecated**)\n\nType: &#96;any&#96;\n\nDefine the default value of the argType. Deprecated in favor of defining the arg value directly.\n\nExample.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Example } from './Example';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Example,\n  argTypes: {\n    value: {\n      // ❌ Deprecated\n      defaultValue: 0,\n    },\n  },\n  // ✅ Do this instead\n  args: {\n    value: 0,\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Example\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWas this page useful?\n\n👍👎\n\n✍️ Edit on Github\n\nOn this page\n\nJoin the community\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,044 developers and counting\n\nWhy\n\nWhy StorybookComponent driven UI\n\nDocs\n\nGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunity\n\nAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcase\n\nExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",

Accessibility tests  \n   * Visual tests  \n   * Snapshot tests  \n   * Test coverage  \n   * In CI  \n   * Integrations\n* Docs  \n   * Autodocs  \n   * MDX  \n   * Doc blocks  \n   * Code panel  \n rendering  \n   * Story layout  \n   * User Interface  \n   * Environment variables\n* Builders  \n   * Vite  \n   * Webpack  \n   * API\n* API  \n   * main.js|ts configuration  \n   * Component Story Format (CSF)  \n   * ArgTypes  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Doc Blocks  \n   * Portable Stories  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * CLI options\n* Releases  \n   * Migrate to Storybook 9  \n   * Migrate from 7 to 8  \n   * Upgrading  \n   * Feature Lifecycle  \n   * Roadmap\n* Contribute  \n   * RFC process  \n   * Code  \n   * Documentation  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * Reproduce\n* FAQ\n\n# Controls\n\nReactVueAngularWeb ComponentsMore\n\nThe &#96;Controls&#96; block can be used to show a dynamic table of args for a given story, as a way to document its interface, and to allow you to change the args for a (separately) rendered story (via the Story or Canvas blocks).\n\n💡\n\nIf you’re looking for a static table that shows a component's arg types with no controls, see the ArgTypes block instead.\n\nScreenshot of Controls block\n\nButtonDocs.mdx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';\nimport * as ButtonStories from './Button.stories'\n \n\u003cMeta of={ButtonStories} /\u003e\n \n\u003cCanvas of={ButtonStories.Primary} /\u003e\n \n\u003cControls of={ButtonStories.Primary} /\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n⚠️\n\nThe Controls doc block will only have functioning UI controls if you haven't turned off inline stories with the inline configuration option.\n\n## Controls\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nConfiguring with props **and** parameters\n\nℹ️ Like most blocks, the &#96;Controls&#96; block is configured with props in MDX. Many of those props derive their default value from a corresponding parameter in the block's namespace, &#96;parameters.docs.controls&#96;.\n\nThe following &#96;exclude&#96; configurations are equivalent:\n\nButton.stories.ts|tsx\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { Meta } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { Button } from './Button';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: Button,\n  parameters: {\n    docs: {\n      controls: { exclude: ['style'] },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof Button\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nButtonDocs.mdx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\u003cControls of={ButtonStories} exclude={['style']} /\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe example above applied the parameter at the component (or meta) level, but it could also be applied at the project or story level.\n\n💡\n\nThis API configures Controls blocks used within docs pages. To configure the Controls addon panel, see the Controls addon docs. To configure individual controls, you can specify argTypes for each.\n\n### exclude\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;parameters.docs.controls.exclude&#96;\n\nSpecifies which controls to exclude from the args table. Any controls whose names match the regex or are part of the array will be left out.\n\n### include\n\nType: &#96;string[] | RegExp&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;parameters.docs.controls.include&#96;\n\nSpecifies which controls to include in the args table. Any controls whose names don't match the regex or are not part of the array will be left out.\n\n### of\n\nType: Story export or CSF file exports\n\nSpecifies which story to get the controls from.
